notes: Each requirement maps a family of frozen verifier assertions (the 7 fixed cases A/B/C/D_cycle/D_selfloop/E/F plus the 25 random-DAG reference trials in tests/test.sh) to the info_slice(s) that disclose the rule the assertion checks. must_include strings are verbatim substrings of the referenced slice content, establishing that info_slices fully cover the instruction, which fully covers the verifier. The case-specific expected numbers are computed by applying these disclosed rules to the fixtures the agent reads from /app/inputs.

requirements.verifier_assertion: test.sh runs `python3 /app/solution.py --input <case_dir> --output <file>` for every case and reads back the written JSON; the tool must accept --input/--output and scan *.json non-recursively.
must_include: reads every *.json file in the --input directory non-recursively

requirements.verifier_assertion: Every case asserts the parsed output has keys status/order/cycle_nodes/peak_live/stats/errors and that status is one of ok/cycle/error.
must_include: status, order, cycle_nodes, peak_live, stats, errors

requirements.verifier_assertion: caseB and caseC assert results computed over the union of multiple fragment files (source_count 2, merged nodes/edges).
must_include: The overall graph is the union of all fragments

requirements.verifier_assertion: Merged-node cases assert the weight chosen by highest priority, ties broken by lexicographically smallest source_id, which the reference uses to compute order.
must_include: the fragment with the highest priority

requirements.verifier_assertion: Cases with edge-only nodes assert those nodes exist with weight null, affecting node_count and ordering (null sorts after numeric).
must_include: created with weight equal to null

requirements.verifier_assertion: caseC asserts edge_count 2 after a duplicate (from,to) edge is collapsed.
must_include: A duplicated edge does not change the edge count

requirements.verifier_assertion: The reference and cases treat weight as a non-negative integer or null, with null a legal value in ready-set ordering.

caseA order [B,A,C,D], caseB [X,Y,Z], caseC [P,Q,R], caseF [H,G,K] and all 25 random-DAG trials assert Kahn's order with in-degree-0 tie-break of ascending weight (numeric before null) then ascending id; order is null when not ok.
must_include: order is the topological order as a list of node ids when status == "ok", otherwise null
ascending weight, where any numeric weight sorts before null
then ascending id as a tie-breaker

requirements.verifier_assertion: caseD_cycle asserts status cycle with cycle_nodes [A,B,C]; caseD_selfloop asserts cycle_nodes [W] for a from==to self-loop; order null in both.
must_include: including any self-loop where from == to
a non-zero remaining in-degree after Kahn's algorithm terminates
cycle_nodes is an empty list in all other cases

requirements.verifier_assertion: caseA/B/C/F assert peak_live 2 via the liveness replay; peak_live is 0 when status is not ok.
must_include: stays live until every one of its direct successors has also been emitted
a node with no successors never counts as live
maximum number of simultaneously live nodes

requirements.verifier_assertion: caseA asserts stats {node_count 4, edge_count 3, source_count 1}; caseB node_count 3 source_count 2 edge_count 2; caseC edge_count 2.
caseE asserts invalid input is detected and that invalidity is checked before cycle detection.
must_include: Invalid input is checked before cycle detection

requirements.verifier_assertion: caseE asserts errors reasons [invalid_edge_endpoint, invalid_node_id] with status error, order null, cycle_nodes [], peak_live 0.
must_include: set status = "error", order = null, cycle_nodes = [], and peak_live = 0

requirements.verifier_assertion: caseA pins order [B,A,C,D], peak_live 2, and stats {4,3,1} together as the canonical example.
